:::{#rem-indefinite-integral-not-shorthand}
#### $\int f(x)\,dx$ has two readings

In calculus,
$\int f(x)\,dx$ with no limits is not a shorthand:
it is the [indefinite integral](calculus.qmd#def-indefinite-integral) of $f$,
a family of functions rather than a number.
Some sources, especially in probability,
also write $\int f(x)\,dx$ for the number $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx$.
Writing the limits out tells the reader which of the two is meant.

:::
